title: The Client Full of Lies
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) omitted by convention. Detective Yokomizo (the investigating officer for this case, analogous role to Inspector Megure but a distinct named character with real plot function -- he physically restrains Kyoko during her suicide attempt and delivers key dialogue) is kept as a person node since he is not one of the four blanket-omitted recurring leads and his actions are load-bearing for the ending. Hattori Heiji and Toyama Kazuha are also kept: the entire 'client full of lies' B-plot only resolves because Ikenami Shizuka turns out to be Kazuha's mother testing Kogoro's competence after Heiji got hurt on a case, which is the actual reason she fabricated her whole cover story (fake reasons for the visit, the dust allergy, disliking cooking, the accidental 'reikoo' Kansai-dialect slip). The old wiki-derived case file (cases/ep220-221_the_client_full_of_lies.json) got the culprit right (Kyoko Shibata) but was otherwise minimal: no murder weapon (bokken), no wedding-ring/bandage staging, no video-timer/breakfast staging mechanics, no book (The Thunder God's Door), no financial/gambling motive, no red-herring accusations against Ikenami and Yoshikawa, and the entire Ikenami/Heiji/Kazuha reveal was missing. case_type: murder.

persons.name: Shizuka Ikenami
aliases: Toyama Shizuka (true identity: Kazuha Toyama's mother)

attrs.true_purpose_of_visit: secretly testing Kogoro Mouri's competence as a detective after her daughter's boyfriend, Heiji Hattori, was injured on a prior case, and because Kogoro never visited or apologized afterward
attrs.cover_story: claimed to be looking for her lost middle-school first love, Shiro Shibata, to retrieve an old photograph
attrs.documented_lies: claimed a dust allergy while actually enjoying cleaning; claimed to dislike cooking while instantly recognizing a fish (guji) by sight; concealed that she was married (bandage hid a mark from a ring on her left ring finger); slipped and said the Kansai-dialect 'reikoo' (iced coffee) instead of catching herself, revealing she was from Osaka
attrs.falsely_implicated: briefly accused of the murder because the victim was found clutching her old photograph; cleared because as an outsider she would not have known the apartment door was already unlocked and would not have passed up the chance to retrieve the photo before police arrived

attrs.note: Kazuha's boyfriend; was injured on a previous case, which is what prompted Shizuka Ikenami to come test Kogoro's detective skill
Shizuka Ikenami's daughter; arrives at the end with Heiji Hattori and reveals Ikenami's true identity and motive

attrs.found_at: hidden behind the stairs near the door

attrs.normal_location: worn on the fourth finger of his left hand

attrs.staging: removed by Kyoko and replaced in his hand with Ikenami's photograph; she likely kept the ring on her own person to dispose of later since she could not risk leaving chemical/blood residue in the apartment

attrs.purpose: concealed the pale mark/indentation left by her own wedding ring, and by extension her marriage to the victim, during questioning; extra bandages placed on other fingers too so the one hiding the mark would not stand out

attrs.history: borrowed by Ikenami from Shiro thirty years ago; she returned it with her photograph left inside as a bookmark
attrs.false_lead: Ikenami claimed a character named 'Reiko' in the book resembled her personality; Conan established no such character exists, exposing another of her lies

clues.desc: The bandaged ring finger vs. the other fingers: only the fourth finger bandage covers an actual injury-free indentation mark, while the surrounding bandages are unnecessary padding meant to make the real one look unremarkable -- comparing the fingers exposes the staging.

Victim's left hand (blood on palm but none on the bandage over the fingers) compared against his right hand (clenched around the planted photograph): the mismatch shows the left-hand bandaging happened after the bleeding, and the right hand's contents were swapped after death -- together they reveal the dying-message photo was staged, not genuine.
